# Sphinteract: Resolving Ambiguities in NL2SQL Through User Interaction

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#sphinteract)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://www.vldb.org/pvldb/vol18/p1145-zhao.pdf) · PVLDB 18(4), print 2024; online record 2025. Author supplement Tables 7-10 also checked.

**Reading coverage:** All 14 proceedings pages: Sections 1-8, Algorithm 1, Tables 1-6, Figures 1-5/captions and references; additional result Tables 7-10 on pages 18-19 of the public author full-paper artifact were read and visually inspected.

**Additional inspected sources:** [Author supplement, Tables 7–10](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ZhaoFuheng/Sphinteract/main/sphinteract_full.pdf#page=18)

## Research question

Identify user-dependent ambiguity and use feedback to refine SQL rather than commit to a single reading.

## Method

Summarize–Review–Ask produces multiple-choice questions with free-form fallback; variants use binary feedback, clarification or early stopping. SQL errors receive an additional repair attempt.

## Evaluation

KaggleDBQA and BIRD experiments use a GPT-4o feedback oracle given gold SQL, with at most four interactions. Eleven SQL-familiar participants separately explore their own intent and then repeat tasks while seeing the gold queries.

## What the results support

The largest reported zero-shot improvement is 42.3 percentage points. Human participants frequently use free-form feedback; the roughly 90% completion result belongs to the gold-visible second phase.

## Limits and qualifications

Benchmark gains depend on reference-informed feedback and hint settings. The small, sequential human study does not validate novice or production use. The ambiguity elicitation study encourages multiple interpretations, so its prevalence is not a general user-population estimate.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Strong evidence for targeted feedback as an interface component, with simulator and human-intent protocols kept separate.
